name: Max Clay
life: “I still remember my first expensive silk ruined by cheap soap.” On Wednesday, near the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, Max prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I bought washable cloth and lied about the price. She made me bring back the receipt.
appearance: Max is easy to recognize by a long plait tucked inside the collar and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a gray fisher's sweater with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining, Max looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
personality: Max keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Max wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To agree the actual cloth price with the client.
family: Grant Tran is Max’s half-sibling. Max chooses an ordinary story to tell. Grant asks the question the rest of the family avoided. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *One last dress rehearsal*, Grant says, “I usually photograph every performance. I put the camera away because the mother wanted her face to be private.”
connections: Alice Brooks. They choose a color the daytime receipt and salon lamp can both explain.

reactions.response: Max leaves the cuff in reach and lets the diner set the pace.
